329209.title: The near-bipartite characterization conjecture for ${\operatorname{LS}}_+$-perfect graphs

literal.statement: For a graph $G$, let $\operatorname{STAB}(G)$ be its stable set polytope, $\operatorname{NB}(G)$ the near-bipartite polyhedral relaxation, and ${\operatorname{LS}}_+(G)$ the Lovász–Schrijver positive semidefinite relaxation. A polyhedron is **polyhedral** if it can be described by finitely many linear inequalities. **The near-bipartite characterization conjecture.** For every graph $G$, the following four statements are equivalent: (1) $\operatorname{STAB}(G)=\operatorname{NB}(G)$; (2) ${\operatorname{LS}}_+(G)=\operatorname{STAB}(G)$; (3) ${\operatorname{LS}}_+(G)=\operatorname{NB}(G)$; and (4) ${\operatorname{LS}}_+(G)$ is polyhedral. This would characterize the graphs on which the Lovász–Schrijver operator reaches the stable set polytope using the near-bipartite relaxation; the paper presents it as an open conjecture.

338330.title: Balog's conjecture on the size of $AA+A$

literal.statement:
Let $A
e
othing$ be a finite set of positive real numbers, and define

$$
AA+A:=\{ab+c:a,b,c\in A\}.
$$

**Balog's conjecture.** For every such set $A$,

$$
|AA+A|\geq |A|^2.
$$

The conjecture was proposed as an analogue of the Erdős–Szemerédi sum-product conjecture. It is refuted by the construction in this paper, which gives arbitrarily large finite sets of rational numbers for which $|AA+A|$ is smaller than $|A|^2$ by a factor involving a power of $\log\log|A|$.

339496.title: Andreae's ubiquity conjecture for locally finite connected graphs

literal.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. For a graph relation $\vartriangleleft$, say that $G$ is **$\vartriangleleft$-ubiquitous** if, whenever a graph $\Gamma$ satisfies

$$
nG\vartriangleleft\Gamma
$$

for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, it also satisfies

$$
\aleph_0G\vartriangleleft\Gamma,
$$

where $\alpha G$ denotes the disjoint union of $\alpha$ copies of $G$. In particular, let $\preccurlyeq$ denote the minor relation. **Andreae's ubiquity conjecture.** Every locally finite connected graph is $\preccurlyeq$-ubiquitous. This is a central open problem in the theory of infinite graphs; although non-ubiquitous graphs are known for some relations, no simple example is known for the minor relation, and it remains open whether a countable connected graph can fail to be minor-ubiquitous.

source.figures: No visual inspection; no figure-dependent ordinary claim

ordinary.analysis: Finite disjoint minor packings need not be nested, so naive diagonal/Konig extraction has no finite-branching hypothesis on ambient Gamma or branch sets. Need a coherent infinite linkage theorem for all locally finite connected G; primary unread.

342461.title: Hanson and Toft's minimum-edge conjecture for Ramsey co-critical graphs

literal.statement:
Let $K_{t_1},\ldots,K_{t_r}$ be complete graphs, let $R=R(K_{t_1},\ldots,K_{t_r})$ be their classical Ramsey number, and let $G$ be a $(K_{t_1},\ldots,K_{t_r})$-co-critical graph on $n$ vertices. The graph $K_{R-2}+\overline{K}_{n-R+2}$ has $(R-2)(n-R+2)+\binom{R-2}{2}$ edges. **Hanson and Toft's conjecture.** Every such graph satisfies

$$
e(G)\ge (R-2)(n-R+2)+\binom{R-2}{2},
$$

with equality attainable for every $n$. Hanson and Toft stated this as the lower-bound counterpart to their sharp upper bound $e(G)\le e(T_{R-1,n})$; the source gives no resolution status for the conjecture.

343194.title: Erdős's conjecture on sparse Steiner triple systems

literal.statement:
For an integer $e\ge 2$, an $(n,3,2)$-design is an $e$-sparse Steiner triple system if it is simultaneously $\mathscr{G}_3(i+2,i)$-free for every $2\le i\le e$. **Erdős's conjecture.** For every fixed integer $e\ge 2$, there exists $n_0=n_0(e)$ such that an $n$-vertex $e$-sparse Steiner triple system exists for every $n\ge n_0$ satisfying

$$
n\equiv 1,3\pmod 6.
$$

The paper reports substantial recent progress, including constructions of $e$-sparse packings, but the stated Steiner-system existence assertion is not presented as fully resolved.

346703.title: Robertson's conjecture on bounded Robertson chains

literal.statement: Let a **Robertson chain** of length $k$ be the graph obtained from a path of length $k$ by duplicating each edge. A graph contains another graph as a **topological minor** if the latter can be obtained from a subgraph of the former by repeatedly contracting edges incident with vertices of degree two. **Robertson's conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$, graphs that do not contain the Robertson chain of length $k$ as a topological minor are well-quasi-ordered by the topological minor relation. This conjecture identifies the known obstruction to well-quasi-ordering graphs under topological containment and is the main objective of the paper; the bounded tree-width case is proved here, while the general conjecture remains open.

348329.title: The removal lemma conjecture for Latin squares

literal.statement:
Let $k,\ell\in\mathbb N$ and let $A\in\mathcal{R}(k,\ell)$. For a Latin square $L$ of order $n$, write $t(A,L)$ for the density of copies of the pattern $A$ in $L$. If entries are replaced by $*$, define $t(A,L^*)$ so that entries marked with $*$ do not contribute.

**Latin-square removal lemma conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that, whenever $L$ is a Latin square of order $n$ with $t(A,L)<\delta$, at most $\varepsilon n^2$ entries can be replaced by $*$ to obtain a matrix $L^*$ satisfying $t(A,L^*)=0$.

This is the direct analogue of the graph removal lemma, but the resulting object is no longer a Latin square because entries have been deleted. The statement is presented as a conjecture and no resolution is supplied here.

literal.statement:
Let $H=(V,E)$ be a hypergraph, and let $I(H)$ be its edge ideal. A **minor** of $H$ is obtained by deleting and contracting vertices. The hypergraph $H$ has the **packing property** if every minor $h$ is König, that is, if its transversal number equals its matching number, $\tau(h)=\pi(h)$. **The packing problem for hypergraphs.** The edge ideal satisfies

$$
I(H)^{(m)}=I(H)^m
$$

for every $m\in\mathbb{N}$ if and only if $H$ has the packing property. This is the combinatorial formulation of the square-free monomial ideal packing problem; its general status is open.

350142.title: Las Vergnas–Meyniel conjecture on Kempe equivalence and graph minors

literal.statement: For a graph $G$, a **$t$-colouring** is a proper colouring using $t$ colours, and two colourings are **Kempe equivalent** when they are connected by a sequence of Kempe changes, each swapping two colours on a maximal bichromatic component. Let $K_t$ denote the complete graph on $t$ vertices, and say that $G$ has no $K_t$-minor when it does not contain $K_t$ as a graph minor. **Las Vergnas–Meyniel's Conjecture A.** For every $t$, all the $t$-colourings of a graph with no $K_t$-minor form a single equivalence class. The paper states that this conjecture is disproved by its construction of graphs with no $K_t$-minor having non-equivalent colourings.

359725.title: Odd-minor clustered and defective colouring conjecture

literal.statement:

$$
\chi_{\star}(\mathcal{G}_H^{\text{odd}})\leqslant 2\operatorname{\overline{td}}(H)-2
$$

and

$$
\chi_{\Delta}(\mathcal{G}_H^{\text{odd}})=\operatorname{\overline{td}}(H)-1.
$$

The paper proves the weaker upper bound $\chi_{\star}(\mathcal{G}_H^{\text{odd}})\leqslant 3\cdot 2^{\operatorname{\overline{td}}(H)}-4$ and places the conjecture as the proposed improvement; its status is not resolved in the source.
